answer: An agent market grants one vote per identity only after 100 credits are locked for 30 days. Validators bind each bond to one public key, hence one vertex in the voting graph, and reject reuse. A tide of aliases hits a basalt floor: each extra fake voter immobilizes another 100 credits. At an assumed 12% annual funding rate, the marginal cost is about 0.99 credits per fake voter per 30 days, even if the collateral is fully returned.
